item.title: Packers Injury Report: 9 players limited on Sunday
item.description: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers had their entire active roster available to practice for the second day in a row. Considering how banged up the roster has been this season, that’s a massive win in itself. The Packers didn’t release a Saturday injury report, though, so Sunday was our first look at details on Green Bay’s injuries. Today, the Packers listed cornerback Brandon Cisse (rib), linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), running back Josh Jacobs (finger), linebacker Isaiah McDuffie (rib), receiver Bo Melton (thigh), receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), edge defender Micah Parsons (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle) and guard Kevin Zeitler (triceps) as limited participants. Cisse, Melton and Moore were unable to finish the game against the Minnesota Vikings last week, while Franklin, Jacobs, Parsons, Rhyan and Zeitler never suited up. The only surprise on this list is that McDuffie is still dealing with a rib injury, as he missed just one snap of action against the Vikings and came back into the game. Guard Aaron Banks is listed with only a knee injury, instead of both a knee and groin injury like in previous weeks, and was a full participant on Sunday. According to head coach Matt LaFleur, Banks is competing at both the left guard and right guard positions for playing time this week. If Banks doesn’t earn a starting role in practice, the assumption is that those gigs will go to Laken Tomlinson (left guard) and Kevin Zeitler (right guard). It’s also worth noting that teams are only allowed three padded practices from Week 12 to Week 18 of the NFL regular season. In preparation for their Week 12 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, the Packers decided to use a padded practice on Sunday. item.title: Best Case, Worst Case, and Most Likely Scenarios for the 2026-27 Badgers
item.description: MADISON, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 10: Owen Foxwell #15 talks with Head Coach Greg Gard of the Wisconsin Badgers during the second half of the game against the Fairfield Stags at Kohl Center on November 10, 2026 in Madison, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images I waited longer than normal to do this piece because the 2026-27 Wisconsin Badgers carried more uncertainty than usual coming into the season, and I’m glad that I did. The first three weeks of the campaign have been both illuminating and disturbing. One big question coming in was whether or not Wisconsin would effectively replace two premium scorers, John Blackwell and Nick Boyd. We all saw an offensive drop-off on the horizon, but how steep it would be was far from certain. There were also associated worries about the lack of a slasher, along with spooky point guard depth. And, of course, fitting the pieces together has always been a puzzle for Greg Gard, who has generally completed it deftly in recent years. Winning the lottery three consecutive transfer portal cycles certainly helped matters. But as we inch toward December, it is clear that this version of the Badgers is flawed and, after losing Jack Janicki to what could be a long-term injury, is now down a major rotational player. Other issues have been a lack of consistent scoring and an oddly passive start from pre-season All-Big Ten senior Nolan Winter, who is very talented but has, at times, looked disinterested on his way to a tepid 8.0 points per game so far , due to a lack of shooting volume. And while they have had nice moments, it’s hard to be overly excited about portal headliner Eian Elmer or new point guard Owen Foxwell . Both have offered flashes, especially Foxwell, but it hasn’t been nearly enough. Making matters worse, transfer big man Victory Onuetu has looked, at times, unplayable. Adding to all this, nobody appears so far to be better than they were in 2026-27, and team cohesion seems broken, as best evidenced by a forgettable two games at the Baha Mar Championship , where the Badgers were outplayed by two decent but not special teams in Seton Hall and Murray State, never looking comfortable and shooting awfully. So, the quick take is that things are not good for Gard’s team and there is a legitimate reason to worry about an awful season. But Gard is a very good coach, and I suspect he will have some fixes to raise the squad’s suddenly troubling floor. However, nothing is a given. item.title: Mark Pope addresses challenges of roster turnover in modern era, building teams for ‘one-year run’
item.description: Since Mark Pope took over at Kentucky in 2024, the transfer portal has been key to building his rosters. He brought in nine players upon his arrival before adding six transfers during both the 2025 and 2026 cycles. The portal landscape has changed recruiting across college sports since transfers gained immediate eligibility. To Pope, it adds to the challenges of roster construction in the modern era, but he also sees some bright spots. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage In the era of player movement, Pope said it’s harder to tell whether a key piece will still be around through multiple years. While Trent Noah is still with the Kentucky program from Pope’s first class, he knows “one-year runs” are becoming more apparent as teams build rosters. “We’re in this era where seasons are standalones,” Pope told Jon Rothstein . “Of course, with everything that changes, you miss some things – you used to be putting together a roster that you would plan out who is going to be around, a particular player, three years from now. There was something great about that and seeing guys grow that way. Listen, we still have third-year guys here at Kentucky that have been with me the whole time. SUBSCRIBE to the On3 NIL and Sports Business Newsletter “But you really, in some essence now, are reconstructing a team for a one-year run in some senses. There’s some really magical things about that, too, is knowing that this is your shot. This is the year that you guys get to be together as an entire group. Taking advantage of every moment and the pace of growth and development and learning, those challenges are really exciting, too.” Last year’s Kentucky team drew plenty of headlines with a roster that reportedly cost upward of $22 million. The Wildcats went 22-24 and lost to Iowa State in the second round of the NCAA Tournament, one year after making it to the Sweet Sixteen in Pope’s debut season. As a result, the 2026-27 season became a big one for Mark Pope in Year 3 at his alma mater, where he was a captain for Rick Pitino . There have been some missteps through the early going, though, as Kentucky heads into Thanksgiving with a 4-2 record. The Wildcats lost to Kansas by 20 points during the Champions Classic and, most recently, had a rough second half in a 90-76 loss to Indiana . They also found themselves in a nail-biter against Northern Arizona at Rupp Arena before coming away with the 78-77 win.

item.description: How Steelers' Loss to Eagles Impacts AFC North Chances, Playoff Path originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Steelers had a fairly favorable path to end a decades-long losing streak in Philadelphia. Instead, they lost their 12th consecutive road game against the Eagles, dating back to 1965. Facing an Eagles team down to its third quarterback, dealing with injuries and subtractions at multiple key positions, the Steelers fell 19-16 on Sunday, unable to generate much offense due to five sacks against Aaron Rodgers and an ejection for DK Metcalf. As Joe Milton did just enough to get Philadelphia a win — its first since Week 2 — Pittsburgh dropped a game that could have some lasting consequences in its AFC playoff chase. Here's an updated look at the Steelers' path to the playoffs after losing to the Eagles. However, considering the Eagles matchup was one of the more favorable ones Pittsburgh had remaining, it does tighten things up a bit for Mike McCarthy's team. Had the Steelers won in Week 11, they would have remained tied in the win column with the Bengals at the top of the AFC North, with Cincinnati still to play on Monday night against the Commanders. Instead, if the Bengals beat Washington on Monday, the Steelers will be two full games behind in the division. item.description: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs ’ offense continued its tear through the middle of the schedule with another 30-plus-point performance, their sixth of the season, against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 11. item.title: ‘Honestly baffling’ – Josh Allen blasted for ‘reckless’ performance in Bills win vs Dolphins
item.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images Josh Allen has come under fire for his shaky performance in the Buffalo Bills’ 26-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon. Allen threw two interceptions against the Bills’ struggling AFC rivals and a third was overturned for a penalty. The 30-year-old finished the game with just one passing touchdown as Buffalo improved to 10-1. His display raised questions about his passing form, particularly against a Dolphins team sitting at 1-8 before this weekend. NFL fans voiced their frustration with the Bills star on social media. One wrote: “Josh Allen hasn’t been a good passer or processor from the pocket for like two years now. It’s honestly baffling.” Another added: “ Josh Allen throwing 3 first-half INTs is nasty work. That 3rd one got called back, but man, the decision-making has been reckless”. A third posted: “Josh Allen has 2 picks against a bad team, with a bad defense, that is also starting a backup QB.” Others were equally unimpressed, with one fan describing it as “Probably Josh Allen’s worst game since the Dolphins game last year.” Another declared: “Safe to say Josh Allen won’t win MVP this season.” Allen has remained in the MVP conversation largely because of Buffalo’s impressive record and his contributions as a runner. He has scored 11 rushing touchdowns this season, but his passing numbers of 14 touchdowns and nine interceptions have not been as convincing. A win is a win for Buffalo, but Allen will need more consistent performances through the air if he is to remain a serious contender for the MVP award. The Bills now face a blockbuster Thanksgiving weekend showdown against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. item.description: Watch Bucky Irving and Vita Vea’s absurd touchdown celebration that has fans going wild originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Vita Vea usually creates highlights on the defensive end, but he went viral for a different reason on Sunday against the Detroit Lions . In the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' loss to the Lions, Vea was a key part of one of the Buccaneers' touchdowns. However, it wasn't the score that went viral, as it was Vea's role in Tampa Bay's touchdown celebration that became a huge hit among fans. In a year that has seen its fair share of creative touchdown celebrations, very few players can celebrate the way that Vea and Bucky Irving did. Take a look at why fans loved this celebration so much. item.title: Jeeno Thitikul three-peats at CME, earning another $4 million check
item.description: NAPLES, FL — Jeeno Thitikul has become a money-making machine . The world No. 2 became the first player to three-peat at the CME Group Tour Championship . In fact, she's the first player to win a tournament three times in a row since Inbee Park won what's now the KPMG Women's PGA from 2013-2015. "I have no word(s)," said Thitikul after a closing 7-under 65 at Tiburón Golf Club. "The only word I have to Terry [Duffy] is just don't change the course until I retire. Don't change it. I mean, it's just me and the course. I think we just really best friend." With the victory, 23-year-old Thitikul surpasses Annika Sorenstam on the all-time money list with $24,292,858. She earned nearly half of that in only three starts at the CME. Nelly Korda, who played alongside Thitikul on Sunday, finished solo third after a closing 68. The world No. 1 also surpassed Sorenstam with a $550,000 check. Korda's career earnings are now $22,972,616. Thitikul, who joined the tour in 2022, accomplishes the feat in only 104 career starts. Sorenstam retired in 2008 and won 72 times. She reached $22,583,693 in 308 starts. "It's really hard to go up against Jeeno out here," said Korda, who has yet to win at Tiburon. "I feel like she just has this place figured out." A victory today at CME would've put Korda into the LPGA Hall of Fame as she's only one point shy of the 27 required to gain entry. Korda won four times this season, including the U.S. Women's Open and Chevron Championship , to earn the LPGA's Rolex Player of the Year award. She battled a two-way miss throughout the week at Tiburon. "You know, still being able to compete when I didn't even really feel like I really had my trust in like a B or C game," she said of her main takeaways. "So just proud of the way that I fought this week to kind of give myself a chance." Thitikul won a tour-leading five times on the LPGA this season, including at home in Thailand, the place where it all began. She made 18 cuts in 20 starts, finishing in the top 10 a total of 11 times (including the wins). The CME check brings her season earnings to $6,923,458. Though she has yet to win a major, Thitikul has said many times throughout her career that her primary goal was to take care of her family, and she has provided well with 12 career victories. Thitikul finished at 24 under for the tournament, two strokes ahead of Japan's Aki Iwai (65), who still won $1 million for her efforts. Miyu Yamashita, a three-time winner this season, won the Vare Trophy with a 69.453 scoring average. Both Nelly Korda and Haeran Ryu were ineligible after failing to meet the required minimum number of rounds. "I'm truly honored to receive this award," said Yamashita. "My goal this season was to win, and I managed to win three times, so overall it's been really good year for me." The countdown to a potential MLB lockout is quickly approaching, with the current collective bargaining agreement set to expire on December 1, 2026. Unless the league and the MLB Players Association reach an agreement, a lockout could begin December 2, bringing baseball's offseason to a sudden halt. The biggest disagreement between the two sides remains the possibility of introducing a salary cap and floor. The timing couldn't be worse for teams looking to make significant offseason moves. item.title: Connor Hellebuyck Hid the Winnipeg Jets’ Biggest Problem for Years. Kyle Connor Is Doing It Again
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kyle Connor has scored 19 of the Winnipeg Jets’ 75 goals this season. That’s 25.3% of the team’s offense through 24 games, which is a pretty ridiculous number for one player to be responsible for. It’s also the sort of statistic that should make Jets fans a little uncomfortable. Connor is doing his job. He’s one of the NHL’s best goal scorers, he’s scoring like one, and nobody is going to complain about having a player who can put the puck in the net almost whenever he feels like it. But when one guy is responsible for more than a quarter of your goals, you have to wonder what happens when he stops scoring at this pace. For Jets fans, this should sound familiar. They spent years watching Connor Hellebuyck turn games the Jets had no business winning into two points in the standings. Sometimes the Jets were genuinely excellent. Other nights, Hellebuyck was the reason nobody cared that they weren’t. The results were great. The problem was figuring out how much of that success was sustainable without him. Now Hellebuyck is in New Jersey, Connor is doing his best to carry the offense, and the Jets are still having trouble controlling play at five-on-five. The more you dig into the team’s numbers from the past several seasons, the harder it becomes to ignore just how much Hellebuyck was making up for. Hellebuyck Was Outperforming Expectations Even When the Jets Weren’t There’s a statistic from the Jets’ 2022-23 season that deserves a lot more attention than it’s received. The Jets finished that year with a plus-11 goal differential at five-on-five, slightly worse than their expected differential of plus-11.55. Nothing especially remarkable there. They scored about as many goals relative to their opponents as the quality of chances suggested they should have. Except Hellebuyck personally saved 22.46 goals above expected. That’s 22.46 goals he prevented beyond what the quality of chances he faced would predict, and the Jets still finished slightly below their expected goal differential as a team. It wasn’t the only time. In 2021-22, the Jets finished 4.95 goals below their expected differential despite Hellebuyck saving 6.28 goals above expected. In 2025-26, the team finished 0.89 goals below expected while Hellebuyck saved another 9.42. Three seasons in which the Jets failed to outperform their expected goal differential despite their starting goaltender beating expectations individually. And when the rest of the team was playing well? That’s when things got ridiculous. The Jets’ Presidents’ Trophy Season Wasn’t Quite What It Looked Like The 2024-25 Jets won 56 games, finished first overall and had the NHL’s best power play. Hellebuyck won the Hart and Vezina trophies, Mark Scheifele scored 39 goals and Connor recorded 97 points. It was the best regular season in Jets 2.0 history, and anybody trying to dismiss 56 wins is being silly. But the Jets’ five-on-five results were considerably better than their underlying number

item.title: Price wins Grand Slam to end wait for major title
item.description: Gerwyn Price has won the Grand Slam of Darts four times [Press Association] Gerwyn Price ended his four-year wait for a major PDC title as he powered to a brilliant 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen in the Grand Slam of Darts final. The Welshman last won a major title when he claimed the World Series in 2022, but finally got over the line after defeats in three finals in 2026. The 41-year-old was the runner-up at the World Matchplay, World Grand Prix and World Series, as well as suffering semi-final exits in the Premier League, World Masters, UK Open and European Championships. This title has been long overdue and Price won it in spectacular fashion with a mid-match burst. Despite six breaks of throw in the opening 14 legs - including brilliant 150 and 145 checkouts from Price - the game was level at 7-7. But Price claimed a crucial lead in a scrappy 15th leg when he finally took out double two at the sixth attempt. That flicked a switch after a mini-interval and Price won the next five legs to open up a six-leg advantage. Van Veen broke back after another interval, but Price was able to hold off any hopes of a comeback from the Dutchman and seal his fourth Grand Slam title. "It's amazing - I've had some close calls this year when I probably should have won games and tournaments, but when it finally comes around it's nice," Price, who moves to world number three, told Sky Sports. "I was probably more nervous in this game than ever. Just to keep the media off my back, I mean I do mind and I don't mind, but just to keep them off my back. "Now they can leave me alone!" The triumph, which sees Price earn £200,000 and the Eric Bristow Trophy, is his first in a PDC ranking and TV major since he won this event in 2021. The pair will now switch their focus to the Players Championship Finals from Friday, where they could meet in the second round. That event will determine Price's place in the PDC order of merit and his seeding for the World Championships which begin on 11 December. The draw takes place on 30 November. Across the 19 editions of the Grand Slam, seven of the winners have gone on to triumph at the World Championship in the weeks that follow. It has happened in each of the past four years, with Luke Littler (twice), Luke Humphries and Michael Smith doubling up. The past 10 years have delivered five winners of both in the same season, while another two Grand Slam winners have reached the Worlds semi-finals and one the quarter-finals. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
